reason: The return plant needs stable ground, so clearing the site with the excavator seems like a useful first step.
expectation: I expect the excavator to prepare or level the plant site, though further work may be needed.

alternatives.reason: The solar modules will likely provide power, but the site seems more urgent.

effect: The excavator graded the site, so I can now prepare its surface.
reaction: That was the expected practical first step.
reason: Ceramic blocks on the graded site seem useful for creating a stable industrial base.
expectation: I expect a paved or supported plant site, though it may need further preparation.

alternatives.reason: Power is also needed, but I want to finish preparing the site first.

effect: The blocks completed the load-spreading footing, and the next goal is power.
reaction: The clear separation from the lander and entrances makes the site feel practically planned.
reason: The spare solar modules need a support structure to supply the plant.
expectation: I expect a mounted solar array, likely needing a cable connection afterward.

alternatives.reason: The cable may be needed for power, but mounting the modules seems like the logical first step.

effect: The spare modules are mounted on an extended solar rack; connecting it is the next apparent power step.
reaction: That was expected, though the result gives little detail.
reason: The power cable should connect the rack to the plant's electrical system.
expectation: I expect a connected solar power supply, although further plant connections may be needed.

effect: The rack now supplies industrial power through its own controller without taking the growing room's allotted power; the chapter is complete.
reaction: The distinction between protected growing-room power and slower fuel production made the outcome more convincing.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the solar rack was most worthwhile: its result tied the new power supply to the existing station and explained the tradeoff in production speed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the solar modules was a predictable intermediate step, and the result gave little detail on its own.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the result to specify that the growing room retained its allotted power while fuel production proceeded more slowly.

arbitrary.text: None of my actions felt arbitrary; grading, load-spreading, mounting and connecting the array all had clear purposes.

continue.text: Yes. The discovery and return plan make me curious about how the local-propellant contingency will work, although this chapter's choices were fairly straightforward.
